title: This leaked Samsung feature might justify paying for Galaxy AI
excerpt: Samsung's Galaxy AI subscription may come with an AI-powered Travel Planner.
content_html:
Published Nov 16, 2026, 9:20 AM EST

I've been covering Android and other mobile technology for close to ten years now, with a specific interest in phone accessories, e-readers, and what makes each individual phone different from another. I delight in looking at the phone market from as many angles as possible, and while my opinions may be odd, at times, they're always from the heart as much as the head. 

I have a background in the mobile accessories world, which explains my odd enthusiasm for cases and things that clip onto smartphones. 

I worked for Digital Trends from 2017 to 2025.

Sign in to your Android Police account

One of Samsung's upcoming Galaxy AI features may be a Travel Planner that helps you to plan for an upcoming trip.

According to the discovered details, this feature will pull from various apps on your phone, and may be powered by Galaxy Claw, an AI-powered feature expected to arrive with the Galaxy AI subscription. Might features like this actually be a reason to subscribe to Galaxy AI?

Travel Planner will automate your travel plans

More actually useful AI features, please

Galaxy Claw is an AI-powered feature that's expected to drop when the Galaxy AI subscription arrives. While details on this are scarce, it's fair to assume it will be similar to the well-known OpenClaw AI agent. In short, it's a locally-run AI agent that acts as a personal assistant, pulling up relevant details and information when needed.

Now, we seem to have details on what exactly Galaxy Claw may be used for, if a leak from The Cipher Project on Telegram is to be believed (via Android Authority).

According to a breakdown of the code contained within the Personal Agent Core app shared in that Telegram channel, Samsung is planning a "Travel Planner" feature. It seems this feature would use Galaxy Claw to pull out data from your emails and calendar in order to create helpful itineraries and plans for upcoming trips.

The idea is clearly to use Galaxy Claw to add more useful AI features that people actually want to pay for. A lot of AI features have been relying on offering answers for problems that either don't exist, or need cater to a very niche set of people. By offering services that help to fit in around your life, rather than trying to impose itself on it, Samsung may have cracked the code on making AI features that people actually want to pay for.

If you, like me, hate planning anything, then the lure of having something do it for you is a strong one. However, there's a strong "use it or lose it" gamble to automating away skills like this, and the chance of ending up like the humans in Wall-E is a possibility.

If Samsung does start including more features like this in its upcoming Galaxy AI subscription, then there's definitely reason for me to pause. My initial, off-the-cuff reaction to Galaxy Ai was to dismiss it, as there wasn't much rumored there that would tempt anyone away from existing similar services offered by Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude. However, if sold well, this sort of feature could appeal to regular people, bringing them into the fold.

Of course, this is all pre-release speculation, and all of this could easily change before launch. Samsung has not confirmed that this feature exists, and it could be completely different by the time it's announced. Hopefully it won't be.
